newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee slows gains as NY eases.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee slows gains as NY eases.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures gave back some gains towards the close on Friday after the arabica futures on the New York market turned sluggish and prices drifted lower on light selling.
Traders said activity was also restricted by players' reluctance to create new positions after a brisk switch-led trade on Thursday.

Earlier talk of LIFFE closing early owing to a power failure also crimped activity. "There was no air-conditioning," said one trader. But the afternoon trading went on as the exchange used back-up generators.
September was actively-traded and ended the day $11 higher at $1,590, its low point, after the day's high of $1,617.
Third-month November was just $10 up at $1,580. Sept/Nov switch was traded at $8-$10.
Volume reached 2,441 lots. The option pit saw a brisk session with 1,132 lots, led by September $1800 calls, changing hand.
Traders said London's fortunes remained hinged on the New York arabica futures which some predicting an encouraging turnaround from the recent spate of losses.
"New York is looking particularly good although the circumstances are different than in London," said one trader. "It will drag London up although the arb between the two will widen."
New York's September formed a double top at 184.50 cents a lb, a resistance which is proving difficult to break. A break at the level will ensure another 10 cent gain, the trader said.
Technically, London's September faces a key hurdle at $1,645 but there is a plenty of overhead resistance beyond that. Support is pegged around $1,545.

Weather-wise, Brazil's meteorologists Somar said a cold front with an intensity of 1024 would be in the Pacific Ocean on July 29 but it was still too early to tell if it would pass Brazil's coffee areas.
"While this highlights that the frost risk has not yet gone away, 1024 is usually regarded as too weak to cause a frost," broker GNI said.
Another trader said: "A frost is still a concern but it's getting less by the day."
